title: Semi-analytical model for the rising sheet generated by droplet-pair impact
summary: When two low-Ohnesorge-number drops impact a dry substrate simultaneously, their spreading lamellae collide and lift a free-standing vertical sheet. The sheet grows by inertial feeding from the spreading drops and is pulled back by capillary retraction at its rim. We develop a semi-analytical model for this rising sheet by extending the single-drop impact description of~\citet{Gordillo2019} to the two-drop geometry. The thin-film flow in the sheet is coupled at its base to the colliding lamellae and at its apex to a capillary-retarded rim. The sheet interior is then solved along ballistic characteristics in two stages: a lamella-fed stage, for which the velocity and thickness fields can be obtained in closed form, and a post-lamella stage, for which the inlet conditions are taken from simulations. The resulting framework gives the three-dimensional velocity and thickness fields and therefore the full sheet shape. On the centreline, the apex height and local thickness are obtained explicitly, showing that the different Weber-number exponents reported in the literature arise from a crossover rather than from a single universal scaling law. At sufficiently large Weber number, the apex pinches off. A linear Rayleigh--Plateau analysis, using the time-dependent jet diameter and deceleration predicted by the model, then bounds the maximum attainable height and closes the description of the pinch-off regime.

AI.tldr: Semi-analytical extension of single-drop impact theory to simultaneous two-drop impacts that form a rising, free-standing vertical sheet: obtains closed-form lamella-fed stage, couples to simulations for post-lamella stage, predicts full 3D velocity/thickness fields, explains different Weber-number scalings as a crossover, and bounds pinch-off using linear Rayleigh–Plateau analysis.
AI.motivation: Understand and model the dynamics of a free-standing vertical sheet produced when two low-Ohnesorge-number drops impact a dry substrate simultaneously, particularly the growth by inertial feeding and capillary retraction, and to reconcile differing Weber-number scalings reported in literature.
AI.method: Extend Gordillo (2019) single-drop model to two-drop geometry. Formulate thin-film flow in sheet coupled at base to colliding lamellae and at apex to capillary-retarded rim. Solve sheet interior along ballistic characteristics in two stages: (1) lamella-fed stage with closed-form velocity/thickness fields, (2) post-lamella stage with inlet conditions from simulations. Use model to get 3D fields; apply linear Rayleigh–Plateau analysis with time-dependent jet diameter and deceleration for pinch-off.
AI.result: Closed-form solution for velocity and thickness during lamella-fed stage; full 3D shape predictions; explicit apex height and local thickness on centreline showing crossover between Weber-number scalings; identification of pinch-off at large Weber number and bounding of maximum height via linear RP analysis.
AI.conclusion: The two-drop semi-analytical framework captures sheet formation and evolution, explains non-universal Weber scaling as a crossover, and, with linear RP stability, closes the description of the pinch-off regime, while relying on simulations for the post-lamella phase and assuming low Ohnesorge number and thin-sheet dynamics.

title: Two-way coupling in active suspensions suppresses particle accumulation and induces non-monotonic flow stabilization
summary: We experimentally study the two-way coupling between a swarm of centimetre-scale active swimmers (Artemia salina) and an electromagnetically driven quasi-two-dimensional cellular flow. The swimmer loading $N$ and the background forcing $E$ are varied independently across 85 conditions, and the coupled dynamics are characterized through Lagrangian diagnostics built on the attracting Lagrangian coherent structures (LCS) of the flow. In the dilute limit, swimmers accumulate onto the attracting LCS most strongly when their speed is comparable to the flow speed, recovering the mobility-selective accumulation predicted by one-way-coupled simulations at the fixed aspect ratio of A. salina. As the loading increases, this accumulation is progressively suppressed, a collective effect inaccessible to single-swimmer models. The back-action of the swarm on the flow is itself bidirectional and regime-dependent: at low forcing the swarm disorders the attracting-LCS web and scatters the topological critical points of the cellular pattern, whereas at high forcing it reorganizes and reinforces the skeleton. The temporal stability of the skeleton is correspondingly non-monotonic in both $N$ and $E$, with the conditions of maximal stability migrating systematically through the $(N,E)$ plane. This reinforcement of coherent structures has no counterpart in prior simulations, which reported a predominantly disruptive back-action. Resolving both directions of the coupling shows how collective activity can either erode or reinforce the transport skeleton of a structured flow.

AI.tldr: Experimental investigation of two-way coupling between Artemia salina swarms and an EM-driven quasi-2D cellular flow across 85 (N,E) conditions, showing mobility-selective accumulation in dilute limit and a regime-dependent bidirectional back-action: disordering LCS at low forcing and reinforcement at high forcing; temporal stability of LCS is non-monotonic in N and E.
AI.motivation: Understand how collective active swimmers modify and are modified by a structured background flow — specifically whether swarm back-action can qualitatively change Lagrangian transport skeletons (attracting LCS) compared to one-way-coupled predictions.
AI.method: (duplicate field not needed)
AI.result: In dilute limit, swimmers concentrate on attracting LCS most strongly when swimmer and flow speeds are comparable (mobility-selective accumulation). Increasing N suppresses this accumulation. Back-action is regime-dependent: low E leads to disordering and scattering of cellular critical points; high E leads to reorganization and reinforcement of LCS skeleton. Temporal stability of skeleton is non-monotonic in N and E, with maximal stability migrating through the (N,E) plane. Reinforcement effect contrasts prior predominantly disruptive simulations.
AI.conclusion: Collective activity produces nontrivial two-way coupling: it can either erode or reinforce the transport skeleton depending on forcing and loading, implying single-swimmer models are insufficient and many-body/back-action effects must be included.

title: The Excess Dissipation of Energy in a Turbulent Boundary-Layer and its Departure from Log-Normality
summary: We investigate turbulent dissipation in a von Karman flow using PIV and Diffusing Wave Spectroscopy measurements to directly compare bulk and wall dynamics. While bulk dissipation conforms to the dissipative anomaly, wall dissipation exhibits a clear excess that grows with Re, consistent with velocity-gradient dominated scaling. Decomposition into dissipation intensity bands reveals that this excess is mainly driven by progressive redistribution toward high-intensity events, larger than 10 x mean, as Re increases. From these measurements, we infer the skin-friction coefficient, finding a decreasing trend with Re fairly consistent with classical power-law behavior despite increasing dissipation. Statistically, the wall shows strong departures from log-normality at low Re that diminishes with increasing Re, reflecting an increase in the effective dimensionality of the near-wall gradient field with Re. In contrast, the bulk dissipation remains near log-normal across all Re with slowly growing log-dissipation variance, consistent with K62 refined similarity. These results suggest distinct origins of log-normal behavior which are multiplicative cascade dynamics in the bulk versus the combined effect of persistent shear and a superposition of an increasing number of independent gradient contributions at the wall.

AI.tldr: von Kármán 유동에서 PIV와 Diffusing Wave Spectroscopy로 벌크와 벽면 소산을 직접 비교했다. 벌크는 소산 이상(dissipative anomaly)을 보이나, 벽면은 Re가 커질수록 증가하는 초과 소산을 보이며, 이는 속도구배 지배 척도와 일치한다. 고강도 이벤트(평균의 10배 이상)로의 재분배가 이 초과 소산을 주도한다. 피부마찰계수는 Re 증가에 따라 감소하며 고전적 멱법칙과 대체로 일치한다. 통계적으로 벽면은 저 Re에서 로그정규성에서 크게 벗어나지만 Re가 증가하면 그 편차가 줄고, 벌크는 모든 Re에서 거의 로그정규를 유지하며 로그소산 분산이 천천히 증가한다. 벌크의 로그정규성은 곱셈적 캐스케이드, 벽면의 거동은 지속적 전단과 독립적 구배 기여들의 중첩으로 설명된다.
AI.motivation: 벽면과 벌크에서의 난류 소산과 간극성(간헐성) 및 스케일링 기원을 구분하고, 특히 벽면 근처 소산 초과와 통계적 분포 차이를 실험적으로 규명하여 이론(예: K62)과의 관계를 밝히려는 목적.
AI.method: von Kármán 장치에서 서로 다른 Re 범위에 대해 PIV(벌크)와 Diffusing Wave Spectroscopy(벽 근처)로 속도 및 속도구배 측정. 소산을 강도 밴드로 분해해서 고강도 사건의 기여를 정량화. 측정으로부터 피부마찰계수 추정. 통계분포(로그정규성, 분산) 및 Re 의존성 분석.
AI.result: 1) 벌크 소산: dissipative anomaly 확인, 로그정규성 근사 유지, 로그소산 분산이 느리게 증가. 2) 벽면 소산: Re 증가에 따라 초과 소산 발생, 고강도 이벤트(>10× 평균)에 의한 재분배가 주 원인. 3) 피부마찰계수: Re 증가에 따라 감소, 고전적 멱법칙과 대체로 일치. 4) 통계적 특성: 벽면은 저 Re에서 로그정규성에서 이탈, Re 증가로 이탈 감소 -> 유효 차원 증가로 해석.
AI.conclusion: 벌크의 로그정규성은 곱셈적 에너지 캐스케이드에 기인하는 반면, 벽면의 통계는 지속 전단과 독립적 고강도 구배 기여의 합성으로 이해되어야 한다. 벽면 초과 소산과 벌크의 소산 이상은 서로 다른 물리적 기원에서 발생한다.

title: An inertial slender-body theory
comment: 41 pages, 23 figures. Submitted to Journal of Fluid Mechanics
summary: We present a fully inertial slender-body theory (SBT) that incorporates the effect of fluid inertia on the scale of the length (the "outer" region) as well as the characteristic diameter (the "inner" region) of a steadily translating slender particle. This is achieved by matching the solution of the quasi-two-dimensional full Navier-Stokes equations in the inner region to an outer solution that consists of a superposition of a solution of the linearized Navier-Stokes equations driven by a line of forces and a potential flow solution driven by a line distribution of sources and source dipoles. The drag and lift forces result from the distribution of Oseen force singularities. These Oseenlets also predominantly govern the torque at small Reynolds numbers and large aspect ratios. However, the potential flow singularities play a crucial role in yielding a torque that grows with increasing Reynolds number at large Reynolds numbers and finite aspect ratios. By comparing the forces and torque on the steadily translating particle with those obtained from a finite difference Navier-Stokes solution, we demonstrate the accuracy of the resulting inertial SBT for $\mathrm{Re}_D$ up to 10, where $\mathrm{Re}_D$ is the Reynolds number based on the smallest dimension, i.e., the characteristic cross-sectional diameter of the slender particle.

AI.tldr: 긴 가늘막대형(슬렌더) 입자에 대한 유체 관성 효과를 내포한 SBT를 제안함. 내부(직경 규모)에서의 준2D 비정상 Navier–Stokes 해와 외부(길이 규모)에서의 선력 분포에 의한 선형화된 Navier–Stokes 해 및 퍼텐셜 흐름을 매칭하여 항력, 양력, 토크를 얻음. Oseen 특이점(선형화된 부분)이 작은 Re와 큰 종횡비에서 지배적이며, 큰 Re와 유한 종횡비에서는 퍼텐셜 특이점이 토크 증가에 중요함. 수치 유한차분 결과와 비교하여 Re_D(단면직경 기반 Reynolds 수) 최대 약 10까지 정확함을 보임.
AI.motivation: 전통적 슬렌더-바디 이론은 주로 관성 무시(Stokes) 한계에서 개발돼 왔고, 유체 관성(특히 직경 규모의 관성) 효과를 포함한 이론적·계산적 간결한 모형이 필요함. 장축(outer)과 단면(inner) 규모의 관성 효과를 동시에 다루는 SBT 확장이 필요함.
AI.method: 내부 영역에서 준2차원(full Navier–Stokes) 문제를 풀고, 외부 영역에서는 선형화된 Navier–Stokes 방정식(선력선 분포로 강제된 Oseen 해)과 소스·소스 쌍극자에 의한 퍼텐셜 흐름을 중첩해 해를 구성. 두 영역을 매칭하여 Oseen 특이점 분포를 결정하고, 이를 통해 항력·양력·토크를 계산함.
AI.result: Oseenlet 분포로부터 항력·양력과 토크를 도출했으며, 작은 Re와 큰 종횡비에서는 Oseen 성분이 토크를 지배함. 반면 높은 Re(유한 종횡비)에서는 퍼텐셜 특이점이 토크 증가를 유발. 유한차분 Navier–Stokes 결과와 비교해 Re_D≤10 범위에서 이론의 정확도를 확인함.
AI.conclusion: 본 연구는 내부·외부 스케일의 관성을 동시에 반영한 실용적 SBT를 제시하며, 제한된 Re 범위 내에서 힘과 토크 예측에 신뢰할 수 있는 결과를 주지만, 비정상, 곡률·말단 효과, 더 큰 Re 등에는 추가 확장이 필요함.

title: Sodium Allostasis: A New Paradigm for Understanding Cardiovascular Volume Accommodation
summary: Arthur Guyton's classic pressure-natriuresis model posits that dietary sodium challenges induce a transient expansion of blood volume that the kidneys rapidly rectify to restore a strict homeostatic baseline, reducing cardiac output to baseline values despite continued higher sodium diet. While this model remains a cornerstone of medical education, it was established in animal models that included surgical reductions in renal mass. Decades of direct human evidence, including long-term balance and spaceflight simulation studies, show that healthy individuals exhibit substantial, persistent plasma volume expansion and sustained cardiac output elevation during prolonged high-sodium intake with little effect on the mean arterial blood pressure. To reconcile these empirical inconsistencies, we propose "sodium allostasis" as an alternative regulatory framework. We argue that sodium regulation operates via two distinct mechanisms: a strict concentration homeostasis that maintains plasma sodium levels (~140 mEq/L) via dilution, and an allostatic accommodation that can sustain a persistently expanded blood volume and higher total body sodium mass. This paradigm fundamentally reframes salt sensitivity. Rather than a primary defect in renal sodium excretion, salt sensitivity reflects a failure of the vasculature to accommodate expanded plasma volume. Furthermore, human and animal data reveal that this chronic allostatic state carries a hidden, profound metabolic cost, forcing energy-intensive sodium reabsorption into poorly oxygenated renal medullary segments and inducing tissue hypoxia independent of blood pressure. Shifting focus from rigid homeostatic volume regulation to vascular accommodation and sodium allostasis provides an accurate physiological foundation for cardiovascular medicine and opens novel, vascular-targeted therapeutic pathways for hypertension and volume disorders.

AI.tldr: 저자들은 혈압-나트륨 배설 모델(Arthur Guyton)이 동물·수술 모델에 기반하여 인간의 만성 고염식 섭취시 관찰되는 지속적 혈장량·심박출량 증대를 설명하지 못한다고 지적하고, 이를 대신할 ‘나트륨 알로스타시스’(sodium allostasis) 개념을 제안한다. 혈장나트륨 농도는 희석으로 엄격히 유지되지만, 총체적 체수분·나트륨량은 장기간 확장될 수 있으며 이것이 혈관의 수용능력 실패(=염분 민감성)의 본질임을 주장한다. 또한 만성 확장은 신장수질 산소저하라는 대사적 비용을 초래한다.
AI.motivation: Guyton의 압력-나트륨 배설 모델과 인간 장기섭취 관찰(장기간 균형·우주비행 시뮬레이션 등) 간의 경험적 불일치를 해소하고, 염분 민감성 및 고혈압 병태생리를 재해석하기 위해.
AI.method: 문헌과 인간·동물의 장기 밸런스 데이터, 임상·시뮬레이션 연구 결과의 통합적 재해석을 기반으로 개념적 모델(‘나트륨 알로스타시스’)을 제안. 기존 모델의 전제(신장 질량 감소 동물실험 등)와 인간 자료를 비교·대조함.
AI.result: 두 가지 조절 메커니즘을 제시: (1) 혈중 나트륨 농도에 대한 엄격한 희석성 항상성(≈140 mEq/L), (2) 혈관 수용으로 인한 지속적 혈장량·총체적 나트륨량의 알로스타시스. 염분 민감성은 신장 배설능력 결함이 아니라 혈관의 확장·수용 실패로 재정의됨. 장기 확장은 신장 수질의 대사적 부담(산소 결핍)을 초래하며 이는 혈압과 무관하게 조직 손상을 유발할 수 있음.
AI.conclusion: 체액·나트륨 조절을 단일한 엄격한 용량 항상성으로 보던 관점을 버리고, 혈관 수용능력과 나트륨 알로스타시스를 중심으로 재구성하면 고혈압 및 체액장애의 병태생리 이해가 개선되고 새로운 혈관표적 치료전략 개발로 이어질 수 있다.

title: Spectral Diffusion for Protein Dynamics
summary: Generative models present a promising alternative to expensive molecular dynamics for computationally querying protein dynamics, yet many existing approaches treat ensembles as unordered snapshots rather than temporally coherent trajectories, or scale poorly with protein size. We present a new physics-informed representation using Fourier transforms as an inductive bias for the multiscale temporal nature of protein dynamics. Diffusion in the spectral domain allows for disentangling of dynamics into slow conformational modes and fast atomic jitter, enabling rapid and improved prediction of dynamics across a range of temperatures. This is facilitated by denoising of structure and temperature conditioned spectral volumes where the low frequencies directly encode per-residue flexibility. Trained on the mdCATH dataset, we evaluate our model, DynaMode, on a held-out test set achieving strong performance across a set of ensemble-based metrics including a Root Mean Squared Fluctuation (RMSF) pearson $r$ of $0.844$. Code is available at https://github.com/HPuntu/DynaMode.

AI.tldr: Physics-informed diffusion model (DynaMode) that uses Fourier/spectral-domain representation to model multiscale protein dynamics, separating slow conformational modes and fast atomic jitter; trained on mdCATH and achieves RMSF Pearson r = 0.844 on held-out test set.
AI.motivation: Molecular dynamics is computationally expensive; many generative approaches ignore temporal coherence or scale poorly. Need methods that capture multiscale temporal structure (slow modes vs fast jitter) and scale to realistic proteins while enabling rapid sampling across temperatures.
AI.method: Introduce a Fourier/spectral-domain representation as an inductive bias for temporal multiscale structure. Apply diffusion in spectral domain with denoising of structure and temperature-conditioned spectral volumes. Low-frequency components encode per-residue flexibility; model produces temporally coherent ensemble trajectories by disentangling slow and fast dynamics.
AI.result: Trained on mdCATH dataset. Evaluated on held-out test set using ensemble metrics; reported strong performance including RMSF Pearson r = 0.844. Model named DynaMode. Code released at github.com/HPuntu/DynaMode.
AI.conclusion: Spectral-domain, physics-informed diffusion enables rapid, improved prediction of protein dynamics across temperatures by separating slow conformational modes from fast atomic jitter; DynaMode is a promising generative alternative to MD with good empirical performance.

title: Body Habitus Dominates Solver Choice as a Source of Uncertainty in MRI Safety Assessment of Active Implantable Medical Devices
summary: MRI is increasingly critical for patients with active implantable medical devices (AIMDs), yet access depends on safety labeling derived from computational heating predictions under ISO/TS 10974 Tier 3. Published assessments have relied predominantly on a single electromagnetic solver class and one or two standard-BMI reference anatomies, leaving the relative contributions of solver choice, tissue property uncertainty, and patient anatomy to predictive variability uncharacterized within a common workflow. We performed a cross-platform evaluation of finite-difference time-domain (FDTD, Sim4Life) and finite element method (FEM, ANSYS HFSS) implementations of the full Tier 3 workflow for a deep brain stimulation system at 1.5 T, extending the analysis across more than 250 clinically realistic trajectories spanning standard male and female references (Duke, HBM, Ella), an elderly male (Glenn), and elevated-BMI models of both sexes (Fats, Ella BMI 30). FDTD and FEM agreed closely in standard anatomies, with Maximum Allowable B1+ limits converging near 2.6-3.0 uT. The elderly male model produced a comparable limit to Duke, indicating BMI rather than age drives heating variability. Elevated BMI reduced safe B1+ by 19-31% in both sexes, while sex at matched BMI had no significant effect. Geometric morphing approximated the native obese limit, whereas dielectric property sweeps failed to reproduce elevated-BMI heating distributions. Body habitus is the dominant source of predictive uncertainty in Tier 3 assessment, exceeding solver choice, dielectric assumptions, and sex. Anatomical diversity, including elevated-BMI female phenotypes, should be treated as a primary variable.

AI.tldr: Cross-platform Tier 3 MRI heating simulations (FDTD vs FEM) for a DBS system at 1.5T across >250 trajectories and diverse anatomies show solver agreement in standard models but identify elevated BMI as the main driver of heating variability (19–31% reduced safe B1+); sex and solver choice are minor factors.
AI.motivation: Current AIMD MRI safety labeling relies on Tier 3 computational heating predictions but prior studies used limited solvers and reference anatomies, leaving unclear how solver choice, tissue property uncertainty, and patient anatomy each contribute to predictive variability.
AI.method: Implemented full ISO/TS 10974 Tier 3 workflow using FDTD (Sim4Life) and FEM (ANSYS HFSS) for a DBS lead at 1.5T. Simulated >250 clinically realistic lead trajectories across multiple reference anatomies: Duke, HBM, Ella, Glenn (elderly male), and elevated-BMI models (Fats, Ella BMI 30). Compared Maximum Allowable B1+ limits and heating distributions; tested dielectric-property sweeps and geometric morphing.
AI.result: FDTD and FEM produced closely matching results in standard anatomies, with B1+ limits ~2.6–3.0 µT. Elderly male (Glenn) similar to Duke, indicating BMI rather than age drives variability. Elevated BMI reduced allowable B1+ by 19–31% in both sexes; sex at matched BMI had no significant effect. Geometric morphing approximated obese limits; dielectric-property sweeps did not reproduce elevated-BMI heating patterns.
AI.conclusion: Body habitus (elevated BMI) is the dominant source of uncertainty in Tier 3 heating predictions, exceeding solver choice, dielectric assumptions, and sex. Regulatory and labeling practices should prioritize anatomical diversity—especially elevated-BMI female phenotypes—when deriving MRI safety limits for AIMDs.

title: Electric Field Propagation with Spinal Cord Stimulation
comment: Pre print 25 pages, 6 figures with a 6 pages of supplementary material
summary: Spinal cord stimulation is routinely used for the treatment of chronic pain, and is increasingly being investigated for the restoration of movement after paralysis. However, most of our current knowledge on epidural spinal cord stimulation relies on empirical approaches and semi-hybrid models. Hence, optimizing this therapy requires a better theoretical understanding of how stimulation affects the target neural structures. Using the physical properties of tissues combined with an electromagnetic, dielectric, and metallic description of them, we derived the electric field transmission coefficient through a given number of layers of tissue in the spinal cord. We then used this model to calculate the transmission of electric field energy in target neural tissues such as grey or white matter for different pulse width. Simulations suggest that the propagation through the tissues of the spinal cord of an epidurally applied electric field has a complex relationship with the field pulse width. In addition the electric field energy is absorbed at the junction between dura matter and cerebrospinal fluid, and within the cerebrospinal fluid as induced current. These currents hit the different bodies floating within the cerebrospinal fluid, and/or dorsal horn in a very localized region of the spinal cord. The proposed models allow theoretical calculation of the transmission factor for different numbers of layers of tissue within the spinal canal, and for different electric field pulse widths. This eases the prediction of the expected energy reaching each layer of the spinal cord for different tissues, parameters, and electrode configurations, simplifying the optimization of spinal cord stimulation treatment.

AI.tldr: 척수 자극(Spinal cord stimulation, SCS)이 다양한 조직층을 통과할 때 전기장 전달 계수를 유도하고, 펄스 폭에 따른 목표 신경조직(회색질·백색질)로의 에너지 전달을 수치적으로 계산하여 SCS 최적화를 돕는다.
AI.motivation: SCS의 임상 적용과 운동 복원 응용이 증가하고 있으나 현재 모델링은 경험적·반하이브리드에 의존하여 이론적 이해가 부족하다. 치료 최적화를 위해 자극이 표적 신경구조에 어떻게 영향을 주는지에 대한 물리적·전기적 해석이 필요하다.
AI.method: 조직의 물리적 특성과 전자기·유전·금속적 특성을 결합하여 척주 내 여러 층을 지나는 전기장 전달 계수를 유도함. 이 모델을 사용해 다양한 펄스 폭에 대해 회백질·백질 등 목표조직으로의 전기장 에너지 전달을 계산·시뮬레이션함.
AI.result: 시뮬레이션 결과, 경막외(Epidural) 적용 전기장의 척수 내 전파는 펄스 폭과 복잡한 관계를 보였고, 전기장 에너지가 경막-뇌척수액(CSF) 경계 및 CSF 내에서 유도전류로 흡수되어 CSF 내 부유체 및 척수의 국소 영역(예: 등각부)에 매우 국소적으로 영향을 준다.
AI.conclusion: 제안된 모델은 척주 내 서로 다른 수의 조직층과 다양한 펄스 폭에 대한 전달 계수를 이론적으로 계산할 수 있어, 조직·파라미터·전극 구성에 따른 각 층으로 도달하는 예상 에너지를 예측하고 SCS 치료 최적화를 단순화할 수 있다.

title: Pretreatment MRI reveals a latent, molecular-subtype-independent structural phenotype that organizes treatment trajectories and recurrence risk
summary: Pathologic complete response and tumor shrinkage measure whether breast cancer responds to neoadjuvant therapy, but not whether that response was structurally favorable, persistent, or hidden beneath volume loss. We built an outcome-blind longitudinal DCE-MRI manifold from I-SPY2 trajectories to test whether pretreatment imaging carries a structural response phenotype missed by conventional descriptors. The dominant axis of response geometry was not recoverable from the full clinical and genomic stack -- age, receptor subtype, MammaPrint, PAM50, treatment arm, and tumor burden -- but became strongly recoverable once baseline structural entropy was added. A constrained representation mapping recovered the same axes as unconstrained decomposition, establishing the structure as intrinsic rather than a post-hoc interpretation. The phenotype persisted through therapy, and as treatment proceeded the volumetric signal faded while entropy stayed separated -- a crossover from burden to structural persistence. Among complete responders, structurally disordered tumors could shrink more early yet remain structurally disordered, a volumetric deception invisible to endpoint labels. External analyses in UCSF, I-SPY1, and Duke established recurrence relevance under representation-dependent boundaries, and a representation-family commensurability assessment showed why feature-name matching is insufficient: the same label can fail, transport, or entangle with extraction geometry. Pretreatment MRI therefore exposes a structural response phenotype that endpoint-based language leaves invisible -- including, among complete responders, a pretreatment imaging signal of structurally distinct response states that awaits prospective validation.

AI.tldr: Outcome-blind longitudinal DCE‑MRI manifold analysis of I‑SPY2 shows a pretreatment structural entropy phenotype predicting structural response geometry to neoadjuvant therapy that conventional clinical/genomic features miss; volumetric signals fade in therapy while entropy persists; external cohorts support recurrence relevance, needing prospective validation.
AI.motivation: Conventional endpoints (pathologic complete response, tumor shrinkage) measure volumetric change but can miss persistent or hidden structural tumor states that influence outcome. The authors test whether pretreatment MRI encodes a distinct structural response phenotype.
AI.method: Constructed an outcome‑blind longitudinal manifold from DCE‑MRI trajectories (I‑SPY2). Quantified baseline structural entropy and incorporated it into representations. Compared recoverability of dominant response axes with and without entropy versus a clinical/genomic feature stack. Used constrained representation mapping vs unconstrained decomposition to test intrinsicness. Performed external analyses in UCSF, I‑SPY1, and Duke; conducted representation‑family commensurability assessment.
AI.result: The dominant axis of response geometry was not recoverable from clinical/genomic features alone but became strongly recoverable after adding baseline structural entropy. Entropy remained separated through therapy while volumetric signal faded, revealing a crossover from burden to structural persistence. Among pCR cases, some tumors showed early shrinkage yet remained structurally disordered. External cohorts showed recurrence relevance under representation‑dependent boundaries.
AI.conclusion: Pretreatment DCE‑MRI structural entropy exposes a structural response phenotype that endpoint‑based labels miss, indicating potential prognostic value beyond pCR and merit for prospective validation.

title: Stability of gas flow past viscoelastic compliant solid
summary: Stability of a high-speed gas flow past a compliant solid is impacted by two distinct features: high solid-to-fluid density ratio ($ρ_r$), and flow compressibility when flow speeds are comparable to acoustic speed. This study investigates the linear stability of a shear-driven compressible gas flow past a compliant substrate modelled as a continuum Neo-Hookean solid. Numerical solutions of the eigenvalue problem reveal that at high density ratios, the dominant instabilities are the elastic shear-waves of the solid. Our study shows that flow compressibility exerts a non-monotonic effect on the growth rate of the elastic modes; the growth rate increases with increase in Mach number up to $\mbox{Ma} \approx 2$ before subsequently decreasing. Furthermore, for compressible flows, strong thermal-coupling renders the base state highly sensitive to both the solid-to-fluid thermal conductivity ratio and the substrate's bottom-surface temperature. Numerical results demonstrate that increasing the conductivity ratio destabilizes the system, whereas increasing the bottom wall temperature is stabilizing. The stability equations, analyzed in the asymptotic limit of $ρ_r \mbox{Re} \gg 1$, reveals that the fluid-solid system de-couples at the leading order with the elastic modes emerging as a solution of the linear elasticity equations under free-shear condition at the interface. We derive a closed-form expression for the leading-order growth rate of the instability, which shows an excellent agreement with the numerical solution. This expression explicitly quantifies the influence of fluid stresses at the interface, which can in-turn be expressed as integrals of the flow solution isolating the distinct physical mechanisms driving the instability.

AI.tldr: 압축성 전단성 기류가 연성(Neo-Hookean) 기질을 지나는 선형 불안정성 해석에서, 높은 고체-유체 밀도비에서 탄성 전단파 모드가 우세하며 마하수 증가에 따른 성장률은 Ma≈2까지 증가 후 감소한다. 열전달(전도)과 바닥온도가 기저상태와 안정성에 크게 영향한다. ρ_r Re≫1에서 유체-고체 계는 일차 해에서 분리되며, 닫힌형 성장률 근해를 유도해 수치와 잘 일치한다.
AI.motivation: 고밀도 비와 유동의 압축성이 결합된 상황에서 유체-고체 상호작용에 의한 불안정성 기작을 규명하여 항공·우주 및 고속유동 응용에서 표면 변형 및 진동 예측을 개선하기 위함.
AI.method: 선형 안정성 분석으로 유체는 압축성 전단류(아마 선형화된 압축성 Navier–Stokes), 고체는 연속체 Neo–Hookean 탄성체로 모델링. 고유치 문제를 수치적으로 풀어 성장률·주파수 도출. ρ_r Re≫1 극한에서 점근해석을 수행해 선도 항에서의 분리 및 닫힌형 성장률 식을 유도하고 수치해와 비교.
AI.result: (1) 높은 ρ_r에서 우세 모드는 고체의 탄성 전단파. (2) 마하수 효과는 비단조적: 성장률이 Ma≈2까지 증가 후 감소. (3) 유체-고체 열결합이 강하면 기저상태가 전도비와 기질 바닥온도에 민감. 전도비 증가가 불안정화, 바닥온도 증가가 안정화. (4) 점근식이 수치 결과와 우수한 일치성을 보임; 유체의 계면응력 영향은 유동해의 적분 형식으로 명확히 표현됨.
AI.conclusion: 연구는 고밀도 비·압축성 유동 하에서의 탄성 모드 주도 불안정성 및 열결합의 역할을 정량화하고, 점근해를 통해 물리적 기작(계면응력의 기여)을 분리·정리하여 수치결과를 뒷받침함.

title: Rethinking Benchmarks and Models for Enzyme Specificity Prediction
summary: Artificial Intelligence has had a profound impact on the biological sciences, and in particular has accelerated research on protein form and function. Enzymes are no exception: a surge of predictive models have been recently developed to address a range of enzyme tasks. Models addressing enzyme-substrate (ES) or enzyme-reaction (ER) compatibility could be especially valuable for enzyme annotation, biosynthetic pathway elucidation, and biocatalyst retrieval, the central challenge of which is the identification of a true catalyst (or truly compatible reaction) among many similar candidates. While existing models report strong performance on alternative benchmarks, less is known about their capabilities in this regime. Herein, we benchmark four recently released ES and ER prediction models, using tasks and datasets tailored to this setting. We first show that two representative ES prediction models perform near random baselines across two enzyme families when considering enzymes and substrates not encountered during training. To evaluate additional models across a consistent dataset, we next assemble the largest cytochrome P450 (CYP) reaction dataset to date, 2,922 reactions across 768 enzymes, and construct a CYP ranking benchmark requiring the correct enzyme to be prioritized among all CYPs in its native organism. We again find that most models do not outperform sequence-based (BLAST) baselines even after fine-tuning. We finally adapt the bimolecular structure prediction model Boltz to ES prediction by training supervised classifiers on residue-ligand pair embeddings, and show that this approach consistently surpasses the BLAST baselines on our CYP ranking benchmark. Together, our results argue for more discovery-relevant benchmarking and suggest that interaction-aware representations from full biomolecular complexes may provide a promising basis for enzyme prioritization.

AI.tldr: Existing enzyme–substrate and enzyme–reaction prediction models perform well on standard benchmarks but often fail to prioritize the true catalyst among many similar candidates; interaction-aware structure-based embeddings (adapted from Boltz) outperform sequence-only baselines on a large cytochrome P450 ranking benchmark.
AI.motivation: To evaluate how current ES/ER predictive models perform in a realistic discovery setting where the task is to identify the true enzyme (or compatible reaction) among many similar enzymes—an unmet need for enzyme annotation, pathway inference, and biocatalyst retrieval.
AI.method: (1) Benchmark four recent ES/ER prediction models on tasks emphasizing unseen enzymes/substrates; (2) build the largest cytochrome P450 (CYP) reaction dataset (2,922 reactions, 768 enzymes); (3) construct a CYP ranking benchmark that requires ranking the correct enzyme above all CYPs in the same organism; (4) compare models to sequence-based BLAST baselines, including fine-tuning; (5) adapt Boltz (a bimolecular structure prediction model) to ES prediction by training supervised classifiers on residue–ligand pair embeddings.
AI.result: Two representative ES models performed near random on unseen-enzyme/-substrate splits. Across the CYP ranking benchmark most models did not outperform BLAST, even after fine-tuning. The Boltz-derived residue–ligand embedding classifiers consistently outperformed BLAST baselines on the CYP ranking task.
AI.conclusion: Current ES/ER models may be overfitting benchmark conditions and lack discovery-ready generalization; interaction-aware, complex-level structural representations are a promising direction for enzyme prioritization and more realistic benchmarking is needed.

title: Geometry-Consistent Discretization of Local Correlation Equations for the Radon Transform in Clinical CT
summary: In this work, we extend the local correlation equation (LCE) framework of the 2D Radon transform to clinical computed tomography (CT) geometry and propose a set of geometry-consistent discretization schemes. Building upon the dual-center-of-rotation formulation, the 1st and 2nd LCEs are reformulated under circular fan-beam geometry and discretized using finite difference methods aligned with clinical acquisition configurations. The numerical validity of the proposed discretized circular LCEs (cLCEs) is evaluated using projection data generated from clinical CT datasets. Quantitative analysis based on residual error, mean absolute error (MAE), and mean percentage error (MPE) demonstrates strong consistency between both sides of the equations, with the 2nd cLCE exhibiting the highest accuracy. Furthermore, the proposed cLCE framework is applied to sparse-view sinogram interpolation. By refining interpolated projections using a gradient-descent-based scheme without additional regularization, improved reconstruction quality is achieved. Experimental results show that the cLCE-refined projections significantly enhance image quality compared to sparse-view reconstruction and can outperform clinical complete view (CCV) reconstruction under certain conditions. These results demonstrate that the proposed cLCE discretization provides an effective tool for exploiting projection redundancy in clinical CT and has strong potential for sparse-view reconstruction applications.

AI.tldr: This paper adapts the 2D Radon-based local correlation equations (LCEs) to circular fan-beam CT geometry, derives geometry-consistent finite-difference discretizations (cLCEs) for clinical scanners, validates them numerically on clinical projection data, and uses the equations to refine sparse-view sinogram interpolation via gradient descent—producing substantial image-quality gains and in some cases outperforming full-view clinical reconstructions.
AI.motivation: Exploit projection redundancy in clinical circular fan-beam CT by extending LCEs (previously in idealized geometries) to practical scanner geometry and provide discretizations compatible with clinical acquisition so redundancy can be used for sinogram interpolation and sparse-view reconstruction.
AI.method: Reformulate 1st and 2nd local correlation equations using a dual-center-of-rotation circular fan-beam model; discretize them with finite-difference schemes aligned to acquisition sampling; validate numerically using clinical CT projection data and quantify consistency (residual, MAE, MPE); apply equations as constraints to refine interpolated sparse-view sinograms via a gradient-descent update (no extra regularization) and reconstruct images.
AI.result: Quantitative consistency between both sides of discretized equations with the 2nd cLCE showing best accuracy. cLCE-based refinement of interpolated projections substantially improves reconstruction quality over sparse-view reconstructions and can exceed clinical complete-view reconstruction under certain conditions.
AI.conclusion: Geometry-consistent discretization of LCEs (cLCEs) is an effective tool to exploit projection redundancy in clinical CT and is promising for sparse-view interpolation/reconstruction tasks.

title: Reactive oxygen species trigger downward vertical migration in diatom microphytobenthic biofilms as a strategy to cope with oxidative stress
summary: Diatom-dominated intertidal microphytobenthic biofilms experience daily fluctuations in irradiance, which can lead to oxidative stress within the photosynthetic apparatus through the production and accumulation of reactive oxygen species. To maintain photosynthetic efficiency, benthic diatoms have developed protective strategies, including mobilization of the antioxidant xanthophyll cycle and the ability to migrate vertically through sediments. However, mechanistic understanding of signaling pathways underlying migration remains poorly characterized. This study investigated the triggering effect of reactive oxygen species on behavioral and photophysiological responses through the analysis of lipophilic pigments and fluorescence parameters. To this end, two microphytobenthic communities, one with sediment allowing vertical migration and another without sediment restricting it, were exposed to irradiance, cold atmospheric plasma, and hydrogen peroxide stresses. Results showed a consistent downward migration response under all oxidative stresses, highlighting the key role of reactive oxygen species, especially hydrogen peroxide, in triggering this microphytobenthic behavior. Moreover, a difference was observed between the pathways involved in vertical migration and those underlying photoprotective responses. Hydrogen peroxide and cold atmospheric plasma stresses highlighted the necessity for substantial microphytobenthic migration, whereas irradiance induced a specific and controlled response involving engagement of the xanthophyll cycle, acting in synergy with the migration strategy by showing stronger activation when migration was impaired.

AI.tldr: 해조퇴적물 표면의 규조류 마이크로피토벤스(biofilms)는 산화 스트레스(H2O2 등 ROS)에 의해 수직 이동(퇴적층 아래로 이동)을 유발하며, 이 행동은 광보호(자산토필 사이클)과는 부분적으로 다른 경로로 조절된다. 빛 스트레스는 자산토필 사이클을 활성화해 이동이 제한될 때 보완적으로 작동한다.
AI.motivation: 해조퇴적물 규조류는 일중 조도 변동으로 인해 광계 내 ROS가 생성되며, 이로부터 광합성 효율을 지키기 위한 이동 및 색소 기반 보호 기작의 신호경로를 규명하고자 함.
AI.method: 두 종류의 마이크로피토벤스(수직 이동 가능/불가)를 대상으로 조도, 차가운 대기플라즈마, 과산화수소( H2O2 ) 처리를 수행. 지용성 색소(자산토필 등) 분석과 형광 파라미터 측정을 통해 행동(수직 이동) 및 광생리학적 반응을 평가.
AI.result: 모든 산화 스트레스에서 일관된 하향(퇴적층 아래) 이동을 관찰했으며, 특히 H2O2가 이동을 유발하는 주요 신호임을 확인. 수직 이동과 광보호(자산토필 사이클)는 부분적으로 다른 신호경로를 가짐. 조도는 자산토필 사이클을 특이적으로 활성화하며, 이동 제약 시 자산토필 반응이 더 강해짐.
AI.conclusion: ROS, 특히 H2O2가 마이크로피토벤스의 수직 이동 행동을 촉발하는 주요 신호이며, 자산토필 사이클은 이동과 보완적으로 작동하는 별도의 광보호 경로임을 제시함.

title: AirTF: Over-the-Air Token Fusion for Task-Oriented Multi-Modal Token Communications
summary: In the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), transmitting high-dimensional multi-modal sensory data to edge servers for time-sensitive tasks faces severe spectrum bottlenecks. To address this, we propose a foundation model-driven over-the-air token fusion (AirTF) framework for task-oriented multi-modal token communications. Unlike existing schemes for segmentation that rely on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with limited local receptive fields, AirTF leverages vision transformer (ViT) encoders to extract globally contextualized semantic tokens from distributed heterogeneous sensors. By concurrently transmitting these spatially aligned tokens over a shared wireless channel, our framework exploits the superposition property of the multiple access channel to inherently fuse complementary multi-modal semantics (e.g., RGB and infrared) directly over the air. This mechanism significantly enhances spectral efficiency compared to orthogonal transmission. Furthermore, the integration of a pre-trained foundation model provides critical visual priors, effectively addressing the data-hungry nature of ViTs on limited, scenario-specific semantic segmentation datasets. Experiments demonstrate that AirTF consistently outperforms orthogonal transmission and CNN-based fusion baselines across AWGN and fading channels. Additional evaluations under a three-user setting, residual synchronization errors, and imperfect channel state information estimation further confirm its robustness. The source code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

AI.tldr: AirTF는 ViT 기반 토큰 추출기를 센서별로 사용하고, 다중접속 채널의 중첩 특성을 이용해 토큰을 동시 전송하여 공중(Over-the-Air)에서 멀티모달 의미를 융합하는 프레임워크다. 기초(파운데이션) 모델의 사전학습으로 ViT의 데이터 의존성을 완화하고, 스펙트럼 효율과 의미분할 성능을 향상시킨다.
AI.motivation: IoV 환경에서 고차원 멀티모달 센서 데이터(예: RGB, 적외선)를 엣지 서버로 전송해 시간 민감적 작업(의미분할 등)을 수행할 때 스펙트럼 병목이 심함. 기존 CNN 기반 분할/퓨전은 지역적 수용 영역에 한정되어 있고, 직교 전송은 스펙트럼 비효율적임. 따라서 공간적으로 정렬된 의미 토큰을 효율적으로 전송·융합할 필요가 있음.
AI.method: 각 분산 센서에서 ViT 인코더(사전학습된 파운데이션 모델)를 사용해 전역 문맥을 담은 의미 토큰을 추출하고, 이 토큰들을 다중접속 무선 채널을 통해 동시 전송한다. 채널의 선형 중첩을 이용해 공중에서 토큰 융합을 자연스럽게 수행하며, 이후 수신단에서 후처리(디코더 또는 분할기)로 태스크별 예측을 수행. AWGN 및 페이딩 채널에서 성능을 평가하고 동기 오차, CSI 불완전성, 사용자 수 확대 시의 강인성도 검증.
AI.result: AirTF는 직교 전송 및 CNN 기반 퓨전 대비 스펙트럼 효율 및 의미분할 성능(mIoU 등)에서 일관되게 우수함을 보였고, 다양한 채널환경과 비이상적 조건에서도 강건성을 보임.
AI.conclusion: 파운데이션 모델과 공중 토큰 융합을 결합한 AirTF는 IoV 환경에서 대역폭을 절감하면서 의미 중심의 멀티모달 통신·처리를 가능하게 함. 다만 동기화, 전력 제어, 모델 연산 비용, 확장성 등의 실환경 적용 이슈는 추가 연구가 필요함.

title: Contrary to Newtonian trends: Early flow transition and drag enhancement at low to intermediate Reynolds number flows of structured fluids
summary: The flow of structured fluids, such as polymeric and micellar solutions, involves a strong two-way coupling between flow kinematics and internal microstructural dynamics, including polymer stretching, micellar scission, and reformation. These interactions yield complex nonlinear rheological responses, including viscoelasticity, shear-thinning, and thixotropy. In this study, we perform high-fidelity numerical simulations of micellar solution flow past a circular cylinder using the Modified Bautista-Manero (MBM) model, which couples a viscoelastic constitutive equation with a kinetic equation for fluidity to capture reversible micellar breakage and reformation. Model parameters are derived from quantitative fitting of experimental data for the EHAC-NaSal system. Our results reveal substantially richer flow dynamics than in Newtonian fluids under the same conditions. Transitions to unsteady flow occur at significantly lower Reynolds numbers, indicating greater instability driven by microstructural effects. At intermediate Reynolds numbers, micellar flows exhibit quasi-periodic behaviour, contrasting with classical periodic vortex shedding in Newtonian cases. Unlike the monotonic drag reduction in Newtonian fluids, micellar solutions show an anomalous drag increase. Wake characteristics reverse with regime: larger recirculation zones at low Reynolds numbers but more compact wakes in unsteady flows. Lift coefficients and Strouhal numbers are consistently increased. Vorticity fields display pronounced spatial localisation within thin near-wake shear layers. A dynamic mode decomposition analysis reveals coexisting unstable time-decaying and self-sustained modes in micellar flows, whereas only self-sustained modes appear in Newtonian cases.

AI.tldr: High-fidelity simulations of micellar solution flow past a cylinder using the Modified Bautista-Manero model show richer dynamics than Newtonian fluids: earlier transition to unsteady flow, quasi-periodicity at intermediate Re, anomalous drag increase, altered wake size, higher lift and Strouhal numbers, localized vorticity, and coexisting unstable/time-decaying and self-sustained modes.
AI.motivation: Understand how micellar microstructure (breakage/reformation, viscoelasticity, shear-thinning, thixotropy) alters bluff-body flow compared with Newtonian fluids and explain anomalous rheodynamic observations.
AI.method: 2D numerical simulations of cylinder flow using MBM constitutive model coupled to a kinetic fluidity equation; model parameters fitted to experimental EHAC-NaSal data; analysis includes wake metrics, drag/lift/Strouhal, vorticity fields, and dynamic mode decomposition (DMD).
AI.result: Micellar flows become unstable at lower Re, display quasi-periodic regimes and anomalous drag increase, have reversed wake-size trends between regimes, higher lift and Strouhal numbers, pronounced vorticity localisation, and DMD identifies both decaying unstable modes and self-sustained modes in micellar cases (only self-sustained in Newtonian).
AI.conclusion: Microstructural dynamics strongly modify bluff-body hydrodynamics; MBM captures key qualitative and quantitative differences, implying that microstructure-driven instabilities and mode interactions are central to micellar wake behaviour and must be considered in modelling and design.

title: Harmonic-Aware Transformer for Real-Time Catheter Localization in Interventional Procedures of Magnetic Particle Imaging
summary: Magnetic particle imaging (MPI) enables real-time, radiation-free tracking of magnetic nanoparticle-coated instruments, making it highly suitable for interventional procedures. This study proposes a harmonic-aware transformer framework that directly predicts catheter tip positions from raw MPI voltage signals, eliminating the need for image reconstruction and reducing computational latency. The framework incorporates frequency-domain preprocessing to isolate the 2nd to 8th drive-field harmonics, enhancing the signal-to-noise ratio while preserving motion-relevant features. A transformer architecture with six encoder layers and eight attention heads is employed to learn spatio-temporal dependencies across the three receive axes (x, y, z) for accurate three-dimensional position estimation. The model is trained on simulated MPI signals and evaluated on real in vitro datasets under standard, bending, and heartbeat-like motion conditions. The proposed method achieves sub-millimeter localization accuracy, with a minimum L2 error of 0.103 +/- 0.092 mm and mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 0.039 +/- 0.046 mm, 0.054 +/- 0.049 mm, and 0.060 +/- 0.044 mm along the (x, y, z) axes, respectively, for the bending dataset. Across all datasets, the MAE ranges from 0.165 mm to 0.655 mm, demonstrating consistent performance. The optimized inference achieves a latency of 0.55 ms per frame and a throughput of approximately 1800 frames per second, confirming real-time capability. Compared with conventional MPI-guided approaches relying on image reconstruction, the proposed framework provides improved accuracy, reduced latency, and enhanced robustness under complex motion conditions. These results highlight the potential of harmonic-aware transformer models as efficient and scalable solutions for real-time catheter localization in interventional MPI.

AI.tldr: Paper proposes a harmonic-aware transformer that directly regresses 3D catheter tip positions from raw MPI receive voltages (2nd–8th harmonics), avoiding image reconstruction; reports sub-millimeter accuracy and real-time latency (~0.55 ms/frame) on in vitro tests.
AI.motivation: Reduce latency and complexity of MPI-guided interventional tracking by removing the image reconstruction step and exploiting harmonic content of raw MPI signals to improve SNR and preserve motion information for direct localization.
AI.method: Preprocess raw three-axis MPI voltages in frequency domain to isolate 2nd–8th drive-field harmonics; feed the harmonic features into a transformer encoder (6 layers, 8 attention heads) that models spatio-temporal dependencies across receive axes to regress 3D tip coordinates. Train on simulated signals and evaluate on multiple in vitro motion scenarios (standard, bending, heartbeat-like).
AI.result: Achieves sub-millimeter localization (minimum L2 error 0.103 ± 0.092 mm; bending dataset per-axis MAEs 0.039 ± 0.046, 0.054 ± 0.049, 0.060 ± 0.044 mm). Overall MAE across datasets ranges 0.165–0.655 mm. Inference latency 0.55 ms/frame (~1800 FPS). Outperforms reconstruction-based MPI localization in accuracy, latency, and motion robustness.
AI.conclusion: Harmonic-aware transformer models can provide efficient, scalable, and real-time catheter localization in MPI without image reconstruction, with strong accuracy and robustness in vitro; further validation and transfer to in vivo settings recommended.

title: Biological Time, Evolutionary Optimization, and Gauge Coherence: A Thermodynamic Synthesis of the Principle of Biological Time Equivalence
summary: Biological theory usually treats time as an external chronological variable against which growth, aging, and ecological change are parametrized. Yet living systems also generate an internal measure of duration through physiological cycling and irreversible entropy production, and the regularities of allometric lifespan scaling, biological clocks, life-history evolution, ecological synchronization, and disease are ordinarily studied in isolation rather than within a single thermodynamic internal-time framework. The Principle of Biological Time Equivalence (PBTE) proposes such a framework.

AI.tldr: PBTE proposes that organisms have an internally generated thermodynamic measure of time—rooted in physiological cycles and irreversible entropy production—that can unify explanations for lifespan scaling, biological clocks, life-history strategies, ecological synchronization, and disease dynamics.
AI.motivation: Biology typically treats time as an external parameter; many time-related phenomena (lifespan scaling, clocks, life history, synchronization, disease timing) are studied separately. A unified internal-time, thermodynamic framework could reveal common mechanisms and generate cross-domain predictions.
AI.method: Introduce the Principle of Biological Time Equivalence: define internal biological time via physiological cycling and entropy production; relate it theoretically to allometric scaling laws and clock dynamics; synthesize existing empirical patterns under a thermodynamic formalism (conceptual/theoretical synthesis, likely invoking non-equilibrium thermodynamics and metabolic scaling relations).
AI.result: A conceptual framework that maps diverse temporal biological patterns onto a single internal-time axis determined by entropy production and physiological cycling, offering explanations for observed regularities and suggesting testable links across domains.
AI.conclusion: PBTE is a promising unifying hypothesis that requires formal mathematical development and empirical validation; it yields clear, testable predictions about relationships among metabolic rate, entropy production, clock periodicity, lifespan, and ecological synchrony.

title: Mutually Exclusive Multiclass Lesion Segmentation in Neuroimaging: Binary-Guided Weak Supervision with Inter-Class Orthogonality
summary: Weakly supervised segmentation of co-occurring neuroimaging lesion subclasses remains challenging due to overlapping activations, noisy pseudo-labels, and the absence of explicit inter-class exclusivity constraints. We propose BiMEx-MS (Binary-guided Mutually Exclusive Multiclass Segmentation), a framework that decomposes multiclass segmentation into whole-lesion localization and exclusive class assignment: a binary localization module provides a class-frequency-agnostic structural prior confining multiclass predictions within the detected lesion domain, while a multi-exit classification architecture with supervised contrastive pretraining produces multi-scale class-discriminative activation maps aggregated via a class-specific attention network. Inter-class exclusivity is enforced through a tri-partite loss comprising per-class separation, inter-class orthogonality, and binary-multiclass spatial consensus, followed by hierarchical morphological pseudo-label refinement. Evaluated across brain tumor MRI (BraTS 2020, BraTS 2023 SSA) and intracranial hemorrhage CT (RSNA-ICH to BHSD) against sixteen weakly supervised baselines, BiMEx-MS achieves Edema HD95 of 29.56 mm (the only method below 40 mm) and subdural hemorrhage Dice of 0.704, with gains consistently largest on boundary metrics and rare subtypes. Cross-dataset generalization, backbone ablations across six architectures, and uncertainty quantification confirm that structural guidance rather than model capacity drives performance. Code: https://github.com/ashutoshkr45/BiMEx-MS-Neuro.

AI.tldr: BiMEx-MS decomposes weakly supervised multiclass lesion segmentation into binary lesion localization plus mutually exclusive class assignment using multi-exit classification, supervised contrastive pretraining, class-specific attention aggregation, and a tri-partite exclusivity loss, yielding improved boundary accuracy and performance on rare classes across MRI and CT datasets.
AI.motivation: Weak supervision struggles with overlapping activations, noisy pseudo-labels, class imbalance, and lack of enforced inter-class exclusivity in co-occurring neuroimaging lesion subclasses, leading to poor localization and mixed-class activations.
AI.method: Introduce a binary localization module to provide a class-agnostic lesion domain prior; a multi-exit classification network with supervised contrastive pretraining to produce multi-scale class-discriminative activation maps; class-specific attention to aggregate maps; enforce exclusivity with a tri-partite loss (per-class separation, inter-class orthogonality, binary-multiclass spatial consensus); followed by hierarchical morphological pseudo-label refinement.
AI.result: Across BraTS 2020/2023 SSA and RSNA-ICH→BHSD datasets and versus 16 weakly supervised baselines, BiMEx-MS achieved notably better boundary metrics (e.g., Edema HD95=29.56 mm, the only method <40 mm) and high Dice on rare subtypes (subdural hemorrhage Dice=0.704); cross-dataset generalization, backbone ablations, and uncertainty analyses indicate structural guidance—not larger backbones—drives gains.
AI.conclusion: Imposing binary structural priors and explicit mutual-exclusivity constraints with multi-scale discriminative features improves weakly supervised multiclass lesion segmentation, especially for boundaries and rare classes; code is released for reproducibility.

title: Mean-flow-based reduced-order models of turbulent channel flow
summary: Reduced-order models (ROMs) for turbulent flows based on Galerkin projection can achieve reasonable accuracy using equation-based modal bases derived from the linearized Navier-Stokes equations through the controllability and observability Gramians. The use of the modal bases obtained from linearized equations around a mean state has been seen to enhance the first- and second-order statistics in the ROM, but the use of the mean state was not necessarily extended to the equations of motion, as it implies the treatment of the divergence of the Reynolds stresses in the Galerkin projection. In this work, we present a mean-flow-based framework for ROMs in which the projection of the Reynolds stresses is solved through a modified modal basis and the knowledge of the mean flow. This framework achieves turbulence statistics comparable to those of a reference direct numerical simulation (DNS) in a minimal channel at $Re_τ \approx 185$. Short-time forecasting with this framework is assessed, where balanced truncation modal bases outperform controllability modes in ROMs, yielding a reconstruction of the velocity field comparable to the Galerkin projection of proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) modes. This framework can extend analysis based on linearisations around the mean turbulent flow, which became widespread in recent years, to include explicitly non-linear interactions between modes, enabling accurate models at higher Reynolds number.

AI.tldr: 평균 유동(Mean flow)을 기반으로 한 ROM(저차원 모델) 프레임워크를 제안하여 Reynolds 응력의 발산을 평균 유동 및 수정된 모달 기저로 투영 처리한다. 최소 채널(Re_τ≈185)에서 DNS와 유사한 난류 통계 재현을 달성하고, 단기 예측에서 균형 절단(balanced truncation) 모드가 제어가능성 모드보다 우수하며 POD Galerkin과 유사한 속도장 재구성을 보였다.
AI.motivation: 선형화된 Navier–Stokes 기반의 모달 기저(제어가능성/관측가능성 그라미안)는 ROM의 통계 성능을 개선하지만, 평균 상태에 대한 선형화를 운동방정식에 일관되게 적용하면 Reynolds 응력의 발산을 취급해야 하며, 기존 연구는 이를 충분히 해결하지 못했다.
AI.method: 평균 유동 정보를 이용하여 Reynolds 응력의 투영을 처리하는 수정된 모달 기저를 도입한 ROM 프레임워크를 구성. 균형 절단(balanced truncation)과 제어가능성 모드를 비교하고 POD Galerkin과 성능을 비교하여 단기 예측과 통계 보존 능력을 평가.
AI.result: 최소 채널(Re_τ≈185)에서 DNS와 비교해 1·2차 통계가 유사하게 재현되었고, 단기 예측에서는 균형 절단 모달 기저가 제어가능성 모드보다 우수했으며 속도장 재구성은 POD Galerkin 수준에 도달.
AI.conclusion: 평균 유동 주위 선형화 기반 해석을 비선형 모드 상호작용을 명시적으로 포함하도록 확장하여 더 높은 Re에서 정확한 ROM을 설계할 수 있는 실용적 경로를 제공한다.

title: Contextual Cellular Growth (ConCeG) of neural cells for realistic grey matter tissue generation for diffusion MRI simulations
summary:
Accurate interpretation of diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) signals in grey matter (GM) remains challenging due to the complex, heterogeneous, and densely packed cellular environment. Numerical phantoms provide a controlled framework for investigating the relationship between microstructure and diffusion signals, yet existing approaches often lack the morphological realism and multi-cellular organisation required to faithfully represent GM tissue.
  In this work, we introduce Contextual Cellular Growth (ConCeG), a generative framework for creating individual cells or constructing dense, three-dimensional, multi-cellular GM substrates informed by real neuronal and glial morphologies. The method combines topological neuron synthesis with a spatially constrained growth network, allowing for the controlled generation of heterogeneous cellular environments with realistic intra- and extracellular compartments. Synthetic cells are generated using morphological and topological characteristics derived from biological reconstructions.
  We validate the framework through comparisons of structural features with real cellular data, demonstrating strong agreement in branch order, length, angle, and tortuosity distributions. Power spectrum analysis further shows that both intracellular compartments reproduce the spatial correlations observed in biological tissue. Together, these results show ConCeG provides a biologically grounded framework for generating grey matter substrates suitable for large scale diffusion MRI simulation.

AI.tldr: ConCeG는 실제 신경세포 형태를 기반으로 개별 세포와 고밀도 3D 다세포 회백질 기질을 생성하는 합성 프레임워크로, 형태학·위상학 기반 세포 합성과 공간 성장 제약을 결합하여 실험적으로 관찰되는 가지 구조 및 공간 상관성을 재현한다.
AI.motivation: 회백질의 복잡하고 이질적인 세포 구조 때문에 dMRI 신호 해석이 어렵고, 기존 수치 팬텀은 형태학적 현실성 및 다세포 조직화를 충분히 반영하지 못함. 이에 실험적 재현성을 가진 합성 GM 기질이 필요함.
AI.method: 생물학적 재구성을 바탕으로 형태학·위상학적 특성을 추출하여 합성 세포를 생성하고, 공간적 제약을 둔 성장 네트워크로 다수의 세포를 충진시켜 실내·실외 구획을 형성함. 세포 간 이질성, 분지 순서·길이·각·굴곡성 등 분포를 제어.
AI.result: 합성물은 실제 데이터와 분지 순서, 길이, 각도, 굴곡성 분포에서 높은 일치성을 보였고, 전력 스펙트럼 분석으로 실내 구획의 공간 상관성 또한 실제 조직을 재현함.
AI.conclusion: ConCeG는 대규모 dMRI 시뮬레이션에 적합한 생물학적 근거의 회백질 팬텀을 생성하는 유망한 도구임.

title: Relativistic PBTE:Biological Proper Time Along the Worldline
summary: Biological aging is conventionally indexed by chronological time, yet every organism is a physical system tracing a worldline through spacetime, so the time available to its metabolism is not coordinate time $t$ but relativistic proper time $τ$. Building on the established Principle of Biological Time Equivalence (PBTE), whose thermodynamic foundation and aging dynamics are taken here as prior results \citep{TayeBook2026,TayeAging2026,TayeCardiac2026}, we ask how internal physiological time relates to the proper time of physics. The central result is that biological age is an entropy-production functional evaluated along the proper-time worldline, \begin{equation*} A_{\rm PBTE}=\frac{1}{Σ_{\rm ref}}\int_{τ_0}^{τ_1}\dotΣ_p(τ)\,dτ, \qquad \frac{dA_{\rm PBTE}}{dt}=\frac{\dotΣ_p}{γ\,Σ_{\rm ref}}, \end{equation*} where $\dotΣ_p$ is entropy production per unit proper time in the local rest frame and $γ$ the Lorentz factor.

AI.tldr: Biological age is expressed as an integral of entropy production along an organism’s proper-time worldline; its rate with respect to coordinate time includes a Lorentz factor.
AI.motivation: To replace chronological coordinate time with relativistic proper time in quantifying biological aging, connecting metabolism-driven entropy production to a covariant measure of biological age via the Principle of Biological Time Equivalence (PBTE).
AI.method: Starting from PBTE and prior thermodynamic foundations, define biological age as A_PBTE = (1/Σ_ref) ∫_{τ0}^{τ1} dotΣ_p(τ) dτ where dotΣ_p is entropy production per unit proper time in the local rest frame; use dt=γ dτ to obtain dA/dt = dotΣ_p/(γ Σ_ref).
AI.result: Provides closed-form relation linking entropy production, proper time, and coordinate-time aging rate; predicts relativistic time-dilation slows coordinate-time ageing rate by factor γ.
AI.conclusion: A covariant thermodynamic definition of biological age that unifies metabolic entropy production with relativistic proper time; requires clarification of operational definitions (Σ_ref, locality, frame, extensivity) and empirical applicability (non-relativistic limit, measurable predictions).

title: Piecewise Dynamic Diffusion Regularization for Reconstruction of Cardiac Cine MRI
summary: Real-time cardiac cine MRI enables visualization of the beating heart during free breathing, but severe undersampling and motion make reconstruction highly challenging. A central challenge for reconstruction is incorporating powerful priors of cardiac anatomy while remaining computationally efficient. We propose Piecewise Dynamic Diffusion Regularization (PDDR), a reconstruction method that integrates a spatiotemporal diffusion model as a generative prior within a variational reconstruction framework for cine MRI. The model employs dedicated spatial layers to encode anatomical structure and temporal layers to capture cardiac motion learned from gated cine data. PDDR leverages the dynamic prior in a piecewise manner, enabling the efficient use of spatiotemporal diffusion models for processing of long real-time sequences. Experiments on retrospectively accelerated and prospective real-time cine MRI demonstrate that PDDR outperforms classical, unsupervised, and diffusion-based methods, delivering high-quality reconstructions with substantially reduced computation time compared to state-of-the-art baselines. These results highlight PDDR as a practical and scalable solution for free-breathing, real-time cardiac MRI. Code is available at https://github.com/MLI-lab/pddr.

AI.tldr: PDDR는 시공간 확산모델을 변분 재구성 틀에 통합해 호흡 자유 상태의 실시간 심장 cine MRI를 효율적으로 복원하는 방법으로, 긴 시퀀스 처리를 위해 확산 사전(prior)을 조각(piecewise)으로 적용해 고품질 재구성과 계산 시간 단축을 달성한다.
AI.motivation: 실시간 자유호흡 심장 cine MRI는 빠른 운동과 심장/호흡에 의한 큰 움직임, 심한 언더샘플링으로 인해 재구성이 어렵다. 강력한 해부학적·시간적 사전지식을 통합하면서도 계산 효율을 유지하는 것이 핵심 도전이다.
AI.method: PDDR는 시공간(spatiotemporal) 확산모델을 생성적 사전으로 변분 재구성 프레임워크에 삽입한다. 공간 전용 레이어로 해부학적 구조를, 시간 전용 레이어로 심장운동을 gated cine 데이터에서 학습한다. 긴 실시간 시퀀스 처리에는 확산 사전을 조각별(piecewise)로 적용해 메모리·계산 부담을 낮춘다.
AI.result: 회고 가속(retrospective) 및 전향적(real-time prospective) 데이터 실험에서 PDDR는 고전적·비지도·기존 확산기반 방법들을 능가하며, 상태‑of‑the‑art 대비 계산 시간을 상당히 줄이면서 고품질 재구성을 보였다.
AI.conclusion: PDDR는 자유호흡 실시간 심장 MRI에 대해 실용적이고 확장 가능한 해결책을 제시하며, 구현 코드는 공개되어 재현 가능성을 지원한다.

title: Experimental and numerical study of the dynamics of sedimenting pairs of semi-flexible fibers close to attractive `aligned' relative configuration
summary: Dynamics of two short semi-flexible fibers settling under gravity in a viscous fluid are investigated at Reynolds numbers Re << 1. We focus on fibers initially relatively close to each other, and we check if later they approach an aligned horizontal configuration, previously identified numerically (Bukowicki and Ekiel-Jezewska, Soft Matter 46 (2019) 9379) as attractive for symmetric initial conditions of moderately elastic filaments. In our experiments, two semi-flexible ball chains sediment in a highly viscous silicone oil. They are initially straight and close to a parallel horizontal relative configuration. Their motion and shape deformation are recorded using two synchronized cameras. For most of the trials, ball chains stay together, with damped oscillations around the symmetric aligned configuration. For a few initial conditions, the ball chains move away horizontally or vertically. To study the behavior over a longer time, we perform numerical simulations, modeling moderately elastic filaments as chains of identical beads, with the centers of consecutive beads connected by springs and with the fibers' elastic resistance to bending. Different initial positions and orientations are considered. Their dynamics are determined by the multipole expansion of the Stokes equations, implemented in the precise Hydromultipole numerical code. For short times, we observe the similar dynamics of semi-flexible ball chains and moderately elastic filaments. We provide examples of long-time numerical simulations illustrating that elastic filaments close to each other can move away horizontally or vertically, but after a long time, come back and perform damped oscillations while approaching the aligned configuration with almost touching filament ends. We confirm the attractive nature of the aligned configuration of very close semi-flexible sedimenting fibers, even if they are far away from each other.

AI.tldr: 두 개의 짧은 반유연 섬유(볼체인) 침강 실험과 수치해석을 통해, 초기 근접 위치에서 대칭적인 수평 정렬 상태로 수렴하는 '정렬 상태'의 유인성을 확인함. 짧은 시간에서는 실험과 수치가 일치하고, 장시간 수치시뮬레이션에서는 일시적 분리 후에도 최종적으로 정렬 상태로 복귀함을 보임.
AI.motivation: 저Re(<<1) 유체에서 반유연 섬유 두 개의 상호작용과 안정한 배열(특히 대칭적 수평 정렬)의 존재 및 유인성 여부를 실험과 수치로 검증하고, 이전의 수치 결과(Bukowicki & Ekiel-Jezewska)를 실험적으로 확인·확장하려 함.
AI.method: 실험: 실리콘 오일 내에 초기 직선·평행에 가깝게 배치한 두 개의 반유연 볼체인을 침강시켜 동기화한 두 대의 카메라로 변형과 운동을 기록. 수치: 동일 구형 입자 연결 스프링과 굽힘 저항을 갖는 비드-스프링 모델로 섬유를 근사하고, Stokes 방정식의 다중극 전개(Hydromultipole 코드)를 사용해 다양한 초기 위치·방향에 대한 장단기 동역학을 계산.
AI.result: 대부분 실험에서 볼체인은 함께 머물며 대칭 정렬 주위에서 감쇠 진동을 보임. 일부 초기조건에서는 수평·수직으로 분리되기도 함. 수치해석은 초기단계에서 실험과 유사한 동역학을 재현하고, 장시간 시뮬레이션에서는 일시적 분리 후에도 결국 거의 닿은 끝을 갖는 정렬 상태로 접근함을 보여줌.
AI.conclusion: 매우 가까운 반유연 섬유의 경우, 초기 거리와 관계없이 장기적으로 대칭 수평 정렬 상태가 유인적이라는 것을 실험과 수치로 확인함.

title: Beam monitoring for radiotherapy from conventional to FLASH dose rates using Low Gain Avalanche Silicon detectors
summary: We report the performance of low gain avalanche Silicon detectors (LGADs) for instantaneous electron and proton beam monitoring across dose rates ranging from conventional radiotherapy to the FLASH regime, benefiting from the fast response of these detectors of a few nanoseconds. The beam sources provide a dose rate greater than 40~Gy/s through pulses of widths 0.5, 1, 2 and 3~$μ$s for electron beams and 3, 5, 10 $μ$s for proton beams. Two different LGAD devices and silicon diodes are tested, yielding a linear dose response for electron beams up to $\sim$450~Gy/s and for proton beams up to $\sim$12~Gy/s. Beyond the linear regime the response continues to increase with a reduced slope and no true signal plateau is observed, at least up to 1800 Gy/s for electrons and 150 Gy/s for protons. This study contributes towards the instantaneous monitoring of increasingly intense flash beams for radiotherapy using fast detectors such as LGADs since measurements can be performed every fraction of $μ$s.

AI.tldr: LGADs exhibit fast (ns) response and show linear dose response up to ≈450 Gy/s (electrons) and ≈12 Gy/s (protons); above those limits signal keeps increasing with reduced slope and no plateau up to the tested maxima (1800 Gy/s electrons, 150 Gy/s protons).
AI.motivation: Provide instantaneous monitoring for increasingly intense FLASH radiotherapy beams by exploiting LGADs' few-ns response time.
AI.method: Measured linearity and response behavior across dose rates, comparing LGADs and silicon diodes.
AI.result: Linear dose-response up to ~450 Gy/s (electrons) and ~12 Gy/s (protons); beyond linear regime the slope decreases but signal continues rising; no true plateau observed up to 1800 Gy/s (electrons) and 150 Gy/s (protons).
AI.conclusion: LGADs are promising for instantaneous monitoring of FLASH beams due to nanosecond timing and high-dose-rate handling; further characterization (nonlinear mechanisms, calibration, radiation hardness, readout limits) is needed for clinical deployment.

title: Stochastic First-Passage Theory of HIV Viral Rebound Following Latent Reservoir Reactivation
summary: In our earlier work, we modeled the stochastic initiation of HIV rebound by treating latent-cell reactivation as a Poisson-driven process during antiretroviral-therapy (ART) washout, immune modulation, and therapeutic perturbation~\cite{Taye2025CM}. That framework characterized activation survival, cumulative hazards, waiting-time laws, and expected viral-load trajectories. However, the endpoint observed in analytical treatment interruption (ATI) studies is not the hidden time of first successful reactivation. It is the first time at which plasma virus exceeds an assay-defined detection threshold. Here we reformulate post-treatment rebound as a stochastic first-passage problem, with $T_{\rm reb}=\inf\{t\ge t_w:V(t)\ge V_{\rm det}\}$. Successful reactivation events arrive with a time-dependent intensity, and each event seeds an exponentially expanding viral lineage. The total plasma viral load is therefore a Poisson shot-noise process, and rebound corresponds to its first threshold crossing. In the rare-reactivation regime, this crossing is dominated by the earliest successful lineage. Rebound timing then separates into two components: a stochastic waiting time for reservoir reactivation and a deterministic growth delay to detectability. This separation gives a shifted-hazard survival law and yields closed-form rebound-time distributions for constant activation, ART-washout-dependent activation, immune-periodic activation, Cox-process activation, and heterogeneous-reservoir activation. The same formulation also provides a likelihood suitable for the interval-censored sampling structure of ATI trials.

AI.tldr: Models HIV rebound timing as a first-passage problem for a Poisson shot-noise viral-load process, separating stochastic reactivation waiting from deterministic growth-to-detectability and deriving closed-form rebound-time distributions and an interval-censoring likelihood.
AI.motivation: Observed endpoint in ATI trials is time-to-detection, not time-of-reactivation; prior work modeled reactivation as Poisson-driven but did not map to detection timing measured in trials.
AI.method: Treats successful reactivations as a (time-dependent) Poisson process; each reactivation seeds an exponentially growing viral lineage; total plasma VL is sum of independent lineage contributions (shot-noise); rebound is first crossing of detection threshold; analyses in rare-reactivation limit yield shift-hazard survival laws and closed-form distributions for various activation intensities (constant, ART-washout-dependent, periodic, Cox, heterogeneous reservoir); constructs likelihood for interval-censored ATI sampling.
AI.result: Derived analytic rebound-time distributions and shifted-hazard survival laws; provided closed-form cases for multiple activation regimes; produced a likelihood tailored to ATI interval-censoring.
AI.conclusion: Reformulating rebound as a first-passage shot-noise problem links latent reactivation kinetics and within-host growth to the measurable ATI endpoint, enabling tractable inference and clearer separation of stochastic vs deterministic contributors to rebound timing.

title: Motion Estimation Techniques for Volumetric Video Attribute Compression
summary: Point cloud compression relies on techniques to compress both geometry and attributes. Motion-based approaches for dynamic solid point cloud geometry compression within the geometry-based point cloud compression (G-PCC) framework have achieved significant reductions in geometry rate. However, motion-based techniques for attribute compression remain underexplored, making it challenging to achieve significant reductions in the temporal redundancy of attributes. Firstly, this paper proposes a geometry-based inter-coding scheme to compress the attributes of dynamic solid point clouds. Secondly, a graph-based motion-estimation scheme for point-cloud attribute compression is proposed. Thirdly, an interpolation-free fractional-voxel motion estimation method is proposed to refine motion accuracy to fractional-voxel precision. Our experimental results on the MPEG point cloud dataset show that the proposed scheme outperforms G-PCC, GeS-TM, and V-PCC in lossless and lossy geometry conditions. We achieve average bitrate savings of $55.3\%$, $42.3\%$, and $16.5\%$ over G-PCC, GeS-TM, and V-PCC, respectively, under lossy-geometry conditions.

AI.tldr: Proposes a geometry-based inter-coding and graph-based motion-estimation pipeline with an interpolation-free fractional-voxel refinement for attribute compression in dynamic solid point clouds, reporting large bitrate savings vs. G-PCC, GeS-TM, and V-PCC.
AI.motivation: Existing motion-based techniques in G-PCC reduce geometry rate effectively but attribute compression still has large temporal redundancy and is underexplored for dynamic solid point clouds; need for motion-based attribute schemes to lower bitrate.
AI.method: (1) Geometry-based inter-coding scheme for attributes; (2) Graph-based motion-estimation tailored to point-cloud attributes; (3) Interpolation-free fractional-voxel motion estimation to refine motion to sub-voxel precision. Integrated into G-PCC framework and evaluated on MPEG dataset.
AI.result: On MPEG point cloud dataset under lossy-geometry conditions, achieves average bitrate savings of 55.3% vs G-PCC, 42.3% vs GeS-TM, and 16.5% vs V-PCC; outperforms baselines under lossless and lossy geometry.
AI.conclusion: The proposed motion-aware attribute compression approach substantially reduces attribute bitrate for dynamic solid point clouds and is effective across tested baselines, with fractional-voxel refinement contributing to motion-accuracy improvements.

title: Acoustic Loading Beneath High-Speed Flow Over a Compression Ramp at Different Angles
summary: Large-eddy simulations are performed to characterize the pressure fluctuations beneath a hypersonic boundary layer approaching a compression corner. The simulations are carried out at Mach 6.04 and an inlet momentum-thickness Reynolds number of $Re_θ=4340$. The compression-corner angle is varied over $10^\circ$, $20^\circ$, $30^\circ$, and $34^\circ$ spanning attached to strongly separated regimes. The peak root-mean-square wall-pressure fluctuations intensity increases sharply with separation strength, rising by $312\%$ from R20 to R30 and a further $67\%$ from R30 to R34, with the peak located downstream of reattachment. Notably, acoustic loading increases from 140 dB in the approach flow to $\approx177$ dB downstream of reattachment in the $34^\circ$ case. Further analysis reveals that intense intermittent pressure events are concentrated near the shock foot, spatially distinct from the peak acoustic-loading region, where fluctuations are relatively sustained. With increasing interaction strength, spectral energy shifts from turbulence-dominated high frequencies to broadband low-frequency motion. Band-isolated acoustic loading maps reveal high-frequency fluctuations as the dominant contributor across the interaction zone, with low-frequency fluctuations becoming locally comparable in the R34 case near the separation region. Spatio-temporal maps of bandpass-filtered pressure fluctuations reveal downstream convecting Kelvin-Helmholtz structures and upstream propagating pressure waves near the shock foot.

AI.tldr: LES를 사용해 Mach 6.04, 입구 모멘텀 두께 레이놀즈수 Re_θ=4340에서 압축 코너(10°, 20°, 30°, 34°)와의 경계층 상호작용을 조사함. 분리 강도가 커질수록 벽면 압력 r.m.s.와 음향 부하가 급격히 증가(예: R20→R30: +312%, R30→R34: +67%, R34에서 재부착 하류 약 177 dB)하며, 고주파 에너지가 저주파로 이동. 강한 분리에서는 충격발(foot) 근처에 강한 간헐적 이벤트가 집중되고 재부착 하류에 상대적으로 지속적인 고음향 부하가 나타남. 대류성 Kelvin–Helmholtz 구조와 충격발 부근에서의 상류 전파 압력파가 관찰됨.
AI.motivation: 극초음속기 및 고속체 설계에서 충격-경계층 상호작용(SBLI)은 구조적 하중, 열부하, 및 음향/진동 부하에 큰 영향을 미치므로 분리 정도에 따른 압력 변동·음향 부하의 공간적·주파수적 특성을 이해할 필요가 있음.
AI.method: 대형 와동(LES) 수치 시뮬레이션을 수행(Mach=6.04, Re_θ=4340). 압축 코너 각도를 10°, 20°, 30°, 34°로 변화시켜 부착에서 강한 분리까지 범위를 확보. 벽면 압력 r.m.s., 음향레벨(dB), 스펙트럼, 밴드 분리된 음향 부하 맵, 밴드패스 필터링된 시공간 지도 등을 통해 시간·주파수·공간 특성 분석.
AI.result: 분리강도 증가에 따라 최대 벽면 p_rms가 크게 상승(R20→R30: +312%, R30→R34: +67%)하며, 최대값은 재부착 하류에 위치. 접근류에서 약 140 dB였던 음향레벨이 R34 재부착 하류에서 ≈177 dB로 증가. 강한 분리에서는 충격발 근처에 간헐적 고강도 압력 이벤트 집중, 하지만 최대 음향부하는 재부착 하류에서 지속적 변동으로 나타남. 상호작용이 강해질수록 스펙트럼 에너지가 고주파(터뷸런스)에서 광대역 저주파로 이동. 밴드 분리 맵은 영역 전반에서 고주파 기여가 우세하나 R34의 분리영역 근처에서는 저주파도 국부적으로 유사한 기여를 보임. 시공간 지도는 하류로 대류하는 Kelvin–Helmholtz 구조와 충격발 부근의 상류 전파 압력파를 드러냄.
AI.conclusion: 분리강도 증가는 경계층와 전단층의 불안정성·비선형 상호작용을 증폭시켜 벽면 압력 변동과 음향 부하를 크게 증가시킴. 고주파 성분이 전반을 지배하지만, 매우 강한 분리에서는 저주파 불안정성이 국지적·광대역적으로 중요해짐. 설계적·진동·음향 관점에서 재부착 하류와 충격발 주변의 동적 거동을 표적화한 진단·억제 전략이 필요함.

title: Comorbidity Network Analysis Reveals Diagnostic Disparities Between Austrian and Non-Austrian Inpatients: A Population-Wide Cohort Study
summary: International migrants face well-documented barriers to healthcare access, yet the extent to which these barriers shape patterns of disease co-occurrence remains poorly understood. Drawing on a nationwide dataset of approximately 13 million hospital admissions from around 4 million individuals in Austria (2015-2019), we constructed and compared comorbidity networks between Austrian nationals and non-Austrian migrants, matched 1:1 by age, sex, and time of first hospital admission (272,779 per group). Following matching, metabolic and cardiovascular diagnoses, including type 2 diabetes and myocardial infarction, were more common among non-Austrians, while depression was more common among Austrians. Comorbidity network analysis showed that among all disease pairs that differed significantly between groups, 70% showed stronger co-occurrence in Austrian patients and 30% in non-Austrian patients. Distinct sex-specific patterns appeared: Austrian males showed stronger associations between alcohol use disorder and mental health diagnoses, whereas non-Austrian males more frequently presented with acute somatic conditions. Among non-Austrian women, a pronounced cluster of recurrent depression, somatoform disorders, and dorsalgia was observed. We interpret the disproportionately fewer comorbidity links observed in non-Austrians not as evidence of lower disease burden, but as a likely reflection of structural access barriers, including language differences, cultural factors, and crisis-oriented admission patterns, that prevent comprehensive diagnostic assessment, though a contribution from the healthy migrant effect cannot be excluded. These findings stress the need for culturally aware care strategies and earlier identification of high-risk multimorbidity profiles in migrant populations.

AI.tldr: Using Austrian hospital data (2015–2019), the authors matched ~272k migrants to nationals and built comorbidity networks: many disease co-occurrences were stronger in Austrians, with some clusters differing by sex; authors interpret fewer links in migrants primarily as reflecting access and diagnostic barriers rather than lower morbidity.
